title: Reverse classification accuracy: Predicting segmentation performance in the absence of ground truth
relevance: Predicts a SEGMENTATION quality score (Dice) for an image with no ground truth, by training a classifier on that image's own predicted mask as pseudo-truth and testing it against a small reference database that does have labels. Segmentation-native, unlike agreement-on-the-line (ID 153) which is a classification result - and its one requirement, a small labelled reference set, is exactly what we have in 2020. This is the most direct route yet to a per-year quality number for 2000 and 2002, the years STATE currently calls un-measurable. Caveat: developed and validated on medical imaging; transfer to aerial canopy is untested and the reference database would need to span our land-cover variety, not just a few sites.

title: ConfIC-RCA: Statistically grounded efficient estimation of segmentation quality
relevance: Joins the two threads this loop has been developing separately: reverse classification accuracy for ground-truth-free segmentation quality, and SPLIT CONFORMAL PREDICTION for guarantees. The result is a PREDICTION INTERVAL on segmentation quality - the true score lies inside it with a user-specified probability - rather than a point estimate, plus retrieval-augmented reference selection so it needs minimal reference data. That is our deliverable's own statistical shape applied at the year level, and it would let us publish a bounded quality figure for un-labelled years instead of shipping them LOW-CONFIDENCE with no number. Same medical-imaging caveat as ID 157.
